title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 108
paragraphs: During that time, while he was in Sardis, he conceived a passionate desire, it seems, for the wife of Masistes, who was also there. Since she could not be bent to his will by his messages, and he did not wish to use force — out of regard for his brother Masistes, and the same consideration also restrained the woman, for she well knew that force would not be used against her — Xerxes then gave up on all else and set about bringing about the marriage of his own son Darius to the daughter of this woman and Masistes, supposing that if he did so he would obtain her more easily. Having made the betrothal and performed all the customary rites, he went away to Susa; and when he had arrived there and brought the woman into his own house for Darius, then he ceased trying to gain the wife of Masistes, and changing his inclination, conceived a desire for the wife of Darius (who was the daughter of Masistes) and obtained her. The name of this woman was Artaÿnte.
